TN NEET Rank List 2026

NEET UG is a national exam for medical courses in India. TN NEET UG 2026 is the counselling process for Tamil Nadu state. It help students get seats in MBBS and BDS colleges in Tamil Nadu. DME handles this process and uses NEET scores to allot seats. TN NEET Counselling process for state quota has begun after release of merit list. Through counselling process candidates get admission to government & private medical college across state. In Tamil Nadu, there is a special rule for state quota seats. 85% seats are for local students, and 15% for all India.

Documents Required for Tamil Nadu NEET UG Counselling 2026

After the DME TN NEET Result 2026, students should take the following documents for TN NEET seat allotment:

  • NEET scorecard
  • Class 10 and 12 marksheets
  • ID proof
  • Passport size photos

If you do not get a seat in Round 1, wait for Round 2. You can also choose to upgrade in later rounds.

Steps After Tamil Nadu NEET UG 1st Seat Allotment Result?

If your name is there in the first 1st seat allotment then follow the below mentioned steps:

Step 1: Go to college.

Step 2: Meet the admission office. They check documents.

Step 3: Pay fees

Step 4: Get admission slip

Step 5: If fees are high check for scholarships. The Tamil Nadu government has schemes for poor students.

In case your name is not there in the 1st TN NEET UG seat allotment list then wait for round 2. You can fill new choices.

What to Do After Tamil Nadu NEET UG Counselling 2026?

If student get a seat through the TN NEET counselling 2026 in the 1st round, he/she should do these important things on priority:

  • NEET UG 2026 scorecard
  • Class 10 marksheet (for date of birth)
  • Class 12 marksheet
  • Transfer certificate from school
  • Community certificate (if applicable for quota)
  • Income certificate (for fee waiver)
  • Aadhaar card or ID proof
  • Passport size photos (6 to 8)
  • Allotment letter

Tips for TN NEET UG Counselling 2026

  • Check site every day for updates.
  • Fill choices based on your rank. Aim for top colleges first.
  • Talk to seniors about colleges.
  • Prepare documents early.
  • If low rank, look for private seats.
  • Stay calm. Many get seats in later rounds.

Common Mistakes to Avoid in TN NEET Counselling

  • Many students make errors. One is not locking choices. Always lock after filling.
  • Another is missing dates. Set reminders on the phone.
  • Do not pay fees to the wrong account. Use official links.
  • If you have a quota like SC/ST, carry a certificate.

What Happens in Future Rounds of TN NEET UG?

  • Round 2 is for leftover seats. If you got a seat but want better, you can join Round 2.
  • Mop-up round is last. It is for vacant seats.
  • All India counselling by MCC is separate. TN is state level.

Tamil Nadu NEET Cut Off 2026

The NEET cutoff 2026 for Tamil Nadu determines the minimum marks and ranks required for admission to MBBS and BDS courses. The cutoff is divided into

  • 15% All India Quota (AIQ): Managed by the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) for seats open to candidates across India
  • 85% State Quota: Handled by DME Tamil Nadu primarily for state domiciled candidates with reservations for categories like OBC, SC, ST, and EWS

The cut off depends on factors such as

  • Number of NEET applicants
  • Exam difficulty level
  • Available MBBS/BDS seats
  • Candidates’ performance
  • Reservation policies

For 2026 Tamil Nadu offers approximately 14,000 MBBS seats and 3,000 BDS seats across government, private and deemed colleges. The cutoff varies by college, category and quota

Tamil Nadu is a hub for medical education with prestigious government, private and deemed universities. Below are top MBBS colleges based on reputation, infrastructure, clinical exposure and 2026 cutoff trends. The selection considers factors like fees, seats and NEET cut offs

Top Government MBBS Colleges in Tamil Nadu

Why Choose These Colleges?

  • Low Fees: Affordable compared to private colleges
  • Clinical Exposure: Attached to large government hospitals
  • Reputation: Recognized nationwide with strong alumni networks
  • Reservation Benefits: State quota offers advantages for OBC, SC, ST & EWS candidates

Challenges: High competition and mandatory rural service bonds

Top Private MBBS Colleges in Tamil Nadu

Private colleges are options for students with moderate NEET ranks. Fees range from ₹4-7 lakh annually, but infrastructure is modern. Below are the top private colleges

  • Modern Facilities: Advanced labs and hospitals.
  • Scholarships: Some offer financial aid or loan support.
  • Good Exposure: Affiliated with reputed hospitals like Apollo.
  • Lower Cutoffs: Easier to secure seats than government colleges.

Challenges: High fees and varying internship quality. Always check placement records.

Why Choose These Colleges?

  • Merit-Based Admission: No management quota, fully through MCC.
  • High Standards: NAAC-accredited with global recognition.
  • Research Opportunities: Strong focus on medical research.

Challenges: Very high fees and competitive cutoffs for top institutes.

Why is Tamil Nadu Good for Medical Studies?

  • Tamil Nadu has old and new colleges. Education is good. Fees in government colleges are low, about 10,000 rupees per year. Whereas, private colleges can charge from 3 to 10 lakhs per year.
  • Good stay facilities as enough hostels are available in any colleges in cities like Chennai, Trichy.
  • Doctors from TN work all over India and the world.
